author: Khan Academy
description: Matter is anything that occupies mass and takes up space. Matter is made of particles, which have kinetic energy—they are in constant movement. There are three states of matter: solids, liquids, and gases. In solids, particles are packed tightly together. Solids have a fixed shape and volume. In liquids, the particles flow around each other. Liquids have a fixed volume but take the shape of their containers. In a gas, particles move freely. Gases have no fixed volume or shape. When the particles of a system gain or lose kinetic energy, a phase change occurs as one state of matter changes into another.
